headline: Public hearing on $128,000 Gateway TIF funding for Rail Trail engineering; Abbott Court development agreement amendment.
summary: Items include a Gateway TIF funding request for Rail Trail design and an amendment to the Master Development Agreement with LMG-NH LLC for Abbott Court. The agenda also covers the Tax Year 2026 tax rate, the FY27 first-quarter financial report, and the introduction of a new assistant fire chief.

Town Administrator’s Report
November 17, 2026
Public Works:
1) The Very Derry Holiday event is scheduled for Saturday, November 28. There are several
activities planned including a parade at 1pm and official tree lighting at 5pm. Activities
will be held in the downtown area centered around Vets Hall , Adams Memorial and
Benson’s Lawn.
2) The Fall Household Hazardous Waste collection day is scheduled to take place on Saturday
November 2 1 at Nelson Fields in Londonderry 830am to 1230pm. Derry residents are
allowed to participate as part of a long-standing partnership. Residents with questions about
allowable products to dispose of are encouraged to access the Town’s website for further
information.
3) A reminder that the annual parking ban has gone into effect November 15 which prohibits
on-street parking from midnight to 6am every night through April 1. The ordinance assists
DPW crews in attending to snow and ice control efforts.
4) The Transfer Station will be closing early on Thursday, November 19 at 1230pm for the
purpose of allowing employees to attend the annual recognition luncheon.
5) The Transfer Station holiday hours are posted on the Town’s website, please note that the
Transfer Station is closed on Thursday, November 26, but open regular hours 6am to
330pm on both Friday November 27 and Saturday November 28.
Finances –
1) The Town’sassessing and financial staff are in the process of setting the 2025 tax rate in
accordance with the approved budget. The Town Council developed their budget using
the 2024 CPI – U Northeast value of 3.5% maximum increase per the Charter. It appears
that the preliminary valuation is showing an increase of $55 million (0.9%) over last year,
which is reflective in the pace of residential and commercial development being seen at
the Planning and Code Enforcement offices.
Other Community Information -
1) The Town received notification that one of two eligible census tracts selected for
designation under the Opportunity Zone 2.0 program. Census tract 003400 encompasses
the Gateway TIF district and covers the north side of East/West Broadway. Census tract
003500 was selected for Opportunity Zone 1.0, and the Town applied to extend that
2
designation beyond the December 31, 2028 sunset date, but unsuccessful. Opportunity
Zone 2.0 designation is a Federal tax incentive program which investors are encouraged
to invest from other capital resources which shields realized and future unrealized gains
from taxation. This is another option for Derry to attract potential investors for future
development.
2) Crews from the Parks & Rec Department dismantled the playground equipment at
Alexander Carr Park due to the age of the equipment and safety concerns raised. The
Parks Department attempted to find replacement parts, but they were unable to do so
because of the age of the equipment. A RFP is being prepared to purchase new equipment
to be installed in an alternate location, closer to the pavilion. Depending on the lead time
from the manufacturers, the hope is to have the new playground in place for late Spring
2027.

SUBJECT: Supplemental Appropriation – Gateway TIF – Rail Trail Design
PURPOSE
The purpose of this document is to seek Town Council approval of a supplemental appropriation for
engineering services associated with the extension of the Derry Rail Trail between Exit 4A/Folsom Road
and the Londonderry town line.
TOWN ADMINISTRATOR COMMENTS
Town Council is urged to reappropriate funds from the Gateway TIF district to support the goal of
connecting the Rail Trail to Londonderry, leveraging NHDOT funds.
BACKGROUND
The Town of Derry currently owns and maintains approximately 3.5 miles of asphalt-paved Rail Trail
extending from the Windham, NH town line northerly to its current terminus at North High Street in
Derry, where it intersects the limits of the Exit 4A Contract, which is presently under construction.
There are two segments remaining to bring Derry’s Rail Trail to the Londonderry town line: The Exit 4A
Section (400 feet) and the Haley Drive north segment to the Londonderry town line (approximately
1,450 feet).
In 2021 the Town of Derry submitted a Transportation Alternatives Program (TAP) funding assistance
application to construct the Derry rail trail between North High St and the Londonderry town line.In
June 2024 the Town of Derry entered into a TAP project agreement with the New Hampshire
Department of Transportation (NHDOT) for funding assistance for the Haley Drive-north segment
(Resolution 2024-023). Per the TAP agreement, all project costs incurred by Derry are to be reimbursed
by NHDOT at 80%. Based on the FY24 project design and construction estimate of $930,534, the DOT
share would be $744,427 and the Town share $186,106.80.
DISCUSSION
In April 2026, in accordance with NH DOT Local Public Agency (LPA) rules, DPW solicited Statements of
Qualifications from qualified professional engineering firms to provide permitting and design
engineering services to complete the Haley Drive – north rail trail segment. Hoyle Tanner Associates
(HTA) was selected based on their qualifications and experience with the Town of Derry. The Town and
HTA have negotiated a scope and fee schedule.
An engineering services agreement for $128,000 for the primary design work has been submitted to NH
DOT for approval. Based on the 80%/20% split the Town portion would be $25,600. Final engineering
and construction appropriations will be addressed in future appropriations.
FISCAL IMPACT
Staff is requesting a supplemental appropriation of $128,000 from the FY27 Gateway TIF budget and an
offsetting revenue of $102,400 from NH DOT to cover the cost of engineering design. The funding

mechanism is a reimbursement process where the Town covers all costs at 100% and then receives the
80% share upon completion of each milestone.
RECOMMENDED ACTION BY COUNCIL
Staff recommends that the Town Council approve a $128,000 supplemental appropriation in the FY 27
Gateway TIF budget and a $102,400 revenue in the FY 27 Gateway TIF budget.
RECOMMENDED MOTION
See Attached Resolution 26-061
Archival Ref: TC agenda item #26-99
RESOLUTION
Number 2026-061
To Approve a Supplemental Appropriation in the Gateway Tax Increment Financing
District Fund.
WHEREAS, the Town Charter establishes the Town Council as the appropriating authority of
the Town and as such it is empowered by Section 9.6 of the charter to make supplemental
appropriations after the annual budget is adopted; and,
WHEREAS, the Town Council previously established the Gateway TIF District pursuant to
Resolution #2020-015 and revised the boundaries pursuant to Resolution #2021-024; and,
WHEREAS, the Town Council seeks to partner with the New Hampshire Department of
Transportation (NHDOT) to design and construct a rail trail section to connect to
Londonderry; and
WHEREAS, the Town of Derry will be reimbursed 80% through NHDOT funding to facilitate
the design; and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED IN COUNCIL THAT the sum of $ 128,000 shall be
appropriated in the FY 27 budget for the purpose of initiating preliminary engineering. Said
appropriation shall be funded using the accumulated fund balance in the Gateway TIF Fund.
Further, the Town Administrator shall be authorized to transfer all reimbursement proceeds
back to the Gateway TIF Fund
This Resolution has been adopted by two-thirds majority of the entire Council as required by
Charter and shall take effect immediately upon its passage.

INTRODUCTION:
To request authorization to sign an amendment to the existing Master Development
Agreement for Abbott Court redevelopment.
TOWN ADMINISTRATOR COMMENTS
This is simply a procedural extension designed to address timing of Phase I and Phase II
BACKGROUND
An existing Master Development Agreement for Abbott Court redevelopment was authorized on
December 3, 2024 by Town Council with an accompanying resolution #2024-066. Subsequent
amendments were approved on March 26, 2026 under Resolution #2026-015 and September 1,
2026 under Resolution #2026-049. The amended agreement will address the following items:
1) Solidify the timing of the parking availability and space count for the Phase I residential.
2) Bifurcate the timing for closing of Phase I and Phase II.
3) Remove reference to a requirement that the Town would seek to fill a commercial space on
the 1st floor, this was an original idea but no longer applicable.
4) Phase I property transaction will be April 1, 2027 or earlier.
DISCUSSION
This action is procedural as Town attorneys and LMG attorneys are reviewing documents on an
active basis and both parties are amenable to the amendment.

Please see Resolution #2026-063

1. Parking. Section 2.1(c) of the Agreement shall be amended by deleting the last
clause thereof, beginning with “provided, however” and replacing it with the following:
“provided, however, that Town shall make available to Developer a minimum of one (1) parking

calculating the Minimum Parking Count, each studio unit shall be deemed to contain one (1)

Developer upon issuance of a certificate of occupancy fo r the Phase I Structure, and the parking
spaces attributable to the Phase II Structure shall be made available to Developer upon issuance of
a certificate of occupancy for the Phase II Structure.”

deemed to refer to the Minimum Parking Count, and the Parking Garage License Agreement shall

2. Closing. Section 2.2(d) of the Agreement shall be deleted in its entirety and
replaced with the following:
